Not sure if there is any interest but like the title says, I am an officer in an AMA Motorcycle Club in Texas. This specific club is AMA chartered and not considered outlaw. While most of us associate with many of those guys, there is no official affiliation (I.E. support club, funneling of money, etc).

I thought that this might be of interest as the dust from the whole Waco incident is settling yet many of us are still being lumped into the generalization. I'd love the opportunity to clear the air and give some understanding of how non-outlaw clubs operate when compared.

If you are interested, ask me anything!
IAMA Officer in a motorcycle club in Texas - ask me anything!

what is the best bike? and why is it Harley?

ok - a real question this time : )

have you noticed any change in the reaction of others while you're on the road since the Waco incident?

Great question!

what is the best bike? and why is it Harley?

I just moved from an 03 Suzuki Intruder to a '15 HD Low Rider and the difference is night and day. I'm sure there are MANY factors that make the Jap bikes superior but the rumble of the HD, the image and the name make up for it. The smooth ride and ease of handling is amazing on the HD.

have you noticed any change in the reaction of others while you're on the road since the Waco incident?

Absolutely. It has pretty much all been negative. Right after the incident we were sent out mass warnings to be careful if we happened to be carrying knives or weapons. A good amount of my club have their concealed handgun license and at the time there were rumors that ANY weapon being carried by someone in a cut/colors/vest would be considered illegal and apprehended. Tons of misinformation went out due to the publicity.

Directly after the incident I found many people taking pictures of me on my bike. It still happens but not as often. You can tell that people get kind of nervous when there is a group of us, for instance we went to Hooters last night while waiting for one of our buddies and everyone seemed nervous while checking us in their peripherals.

Last week three of us stopped at a CVS while waiting for a buddy. A car full of college age girls was parked next to us when we pulled up, all still in the car. We got off of our bikes and smoked a few cigarettes while waiting for our buddy. The girls did not get out of their car for an entire 20 minutes until directly after we started pulling away. It really isn't a problem but kind of annoying as the majority of us are the complete opposite as to what you see on the news and SOA.

kind of amazing, and disappointing really, that people judge other by what they see on the boob-tube

what about promoting the "likability", if i may, of the clubs by doing something to contrib to the community where you can leverage the media to get some positive exposure?

We actually do a ton of community outreach but do not really have the resources to make it more public. We are the ones doing the huge toy runs and there are a couple of organizations in our area that we support, one being the Texas Lions camp for disabled children. We usually donate 20k-50k yearly to this organization. We also support our local American Legion and VFW.

i think if you want to combat the stereotype, you have to talk to people - this may sound completely dorky, but imagine the potential attention a club might get if it did something a simple as running a lemonade stand?

here's why i think something like this might be a good idea...

  • it's a job associated with kids, so right of way it puts a "cute" light on you
  • it might grab a lot of media attention
  • puts you 1 on 1 with the public
  • could be an instant YouTube hit if done right
  • minimal investment

We also have a few other that we support and donate to (Toy runs, events, etc) but Texas Lions camp is our main.
